text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Peace still a dream. On the eve of every New Year, hopes rise to see Algeria pull out of the crisis, heal wounds and reconcile its sons. But on this last day of 1996, these hopes seem to be not fulfilled even though they will be renewed this evening. The newspaper printed a cartoon showing a man walking towards 1997, a knife in his back and his head smashed by an axe.

- 1996 broke many promises, and three conclusions may be drawn: "terrorism has not been wiped out, people's purchasing power has detriorated and political life faces more restrictions. Liberte published the photograph of a woman hugging her baby daughter, the two of them crying.

- 1996 was a hard, very hard year which ended with massacres and continuing censorship keeping Algerians in the dark about Moslem fundamentalist crimes. The tragedy experienced by our country and our people risks, alas, to continue.
- The year ends with a 4 percent increase in the Gross Domestic Product, nine billion dinars devoted to help the poor, and patent results in the fight against "terrorism".
- Economic development still an everyday struggle and it will be achieved only with consensus in society.
